title: I quantized my MIDI piano and now it sounds robotic. How do I tighten it without killing the feel
canonical_user_question: I quantized my MIDI piano and now it sounds robotic. How do I tighten it without killing the feel?
natural_language_variants: How do I keep rubato and rolled chords?
Should I use Smart Quantize on piano?
clarification_questions: Is the performance supposed to follow the project grid, or should the project tempo follow the performance?
Which musical events carry the pulse, and which are intentional ornaments, rolls, pedal events, or expressive offsets?
Is the timing error systematic, section-specific, or only a few notes?

recommended_first_experiment.summary: Undo/reset quantization, switch to Smart Quantize, and apply partial Q-Strength to a duplicate region.
recommended_first_experiment.why_this_first: Non-destructive duplicate-region comparison protects the original feel and reveals whether the grid or algorithm is the real issue.
recommended_first_experiment.action: Undo/reset quantization, switch to Smart Quantize, and apply partial Q-Strength to a duplicate region.

logic_pro_steps: Duplicate the MIDI region or preserve the unquantized original.
Select the MIDI region, choose Smart Quantize, set the likely rhythmic grid, lower Q-Strength, and compare with the original.
Toggle Quantize Off/On or compare the duplicate at the same instrument and level.
Inspect note starts, note lengths, velocities, and CC/pedal events only after listening.
starting_points: Begin with partial correction and preserve note order; tighten only the passages that distract.
what_to_listen_for: Pulse should become clearer while chord rolls, hand separation, and phrasing remain.
Check both the isolated instrument and its relationship to drums/bass/metronome.
stop_rule: Stop increasing correction as soon as the pulse reads clearly and intentional internal timing remains.
undo_or_reset: Set Region Quantize to Off/reset advanced parameters, restore the duplicate, or Undo note-level quantization.
rationale: Quantization is a relationship between a performance, a grid, and musical roles. The best setting improves the pulse without erasing intentional timing.
tradeoffs_and_risks: More grid precision can reduce groove, hand independence, ornaments, or pedal relationships.
Visual alignment is not the same as musical alignment.
alternatives_if_wrong: Manually fix only the distracting outliers.
Create or use a groove template from a trusted performance.
Build a tempo map when the performance should lead the project.
Re-record the passage when latency or performance confusion is the real problem.
common_mistakes: Applying 100% Classic Quantize to the whole region by default.
Choosing the grid from the smallest accidental note.
Ignoring sustain pedal and other CC data.
Using random humanization as a substitute for groove.
teaching_principle: Quantize anchors and relationships, not every event. Decide what should lead before deciding how much to move.
do_not_assume: One quantize value fits every role in the region.
